answer: Erasure-coded availability proofs split a block into many coded fragments so that any sufficiently large subset can rebuild the original, and a prover must show enough distinct fragments exist. A cipher of coded pieces means losing some fragments is harmless, a quill marking each fragment proves it belongs to this block, and a nectar of redundancy lets verifiers reconstruct from whatever survives. A farm cannot claim many blocks are available while storing only a few fragments of each, because reconstruction needs a threshold of real fragments.
